title: Block close: the hidden light (Chagigah 12a)
hookLine: the light of creation was hidden away for the righteous
last: THE MYSTIC'S CLIMB ENDS IN QUIET KINDNESS.

cards: "And God said, Let there be light: and there was light." That's the first day of creation. Keep reading Genesis and you reach the fourth day, when God makes the sun, the moon and the stars.
So a careful reader stops: if the sun came on day four, what was the light of day one? The rabbis of the Talmud asked exactly that.
Their answer closes this whole block on Kabbalah and Hasidic thought, because it's a story about light that's still here, just out of sight.

teach.h: THE LIGHT OF THE FIRST DAY.
teach.b: The hidden light. First, the passage. In the Talmud, tractate Chagigah, the sages teach that the light of the first day was a different light.
By it, the first human being could see from one end of the world to the other. But when God foresaw generations who would misuse it, God hid it away, set aside for the righteous in the time to come.
Second, a verse that keeps it close.

teach.h: LIGHT IS SOWN FOR THE RIGHTEOUS.
teach.b: The Psalm says: "Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart." Sown, like a seed: hidden, but planted, waiting to come up. Third, where the light went.

Teachings handed down in the Baal Shem Tov's name say the hidden light was tucked into the Torah itself, so whoever studies it with love can catch a glimmer now. That's the whole block in one picture.
You began with the received, and a warning to enter carefully. Letters that create, ten lights, broken vessels, a shard to repair.
Then the Hasidim: no place without him, cling, joy opens, less me, two souls, truth, fiercely, hidden will, a ladder of song, mystic kindness. Fourth, the thread running through them.
Again and again, these teachings say the light didn't leave.
It's hidden, scattered, sown, waiting in a page, a song, a stove before dawn. Next comes a new block: the movements of modern Jewish life, side by side, without ranking.

how: Jews read the creation story aloud in synagogue when the Torah reading cycle begins again, and the Talmud's teaching on the hidden light is studied in Chagigah and retold in kabbalistic and Hasidic teaching.

the Talmud says the first human could see from one end of the world to the other by that light

games.q: God foresees generations who would misuse the light of the first day. what does God do with it, says the Talmud?
o: hides it away for the righteous.
games.why: the sages say God set it aside for the righteous in the time to come. Hasidic teaching adds that it was tucked into the Torah.

practice: Think back across the last few weeks and find one moment when something good showed up where you didn't expect it: a kind word, a song, a person who stayed. Let it brighten in your mind for a few breaths.
Then rest your gaze on one ordinary thing near you, a cup, a window, a hand, and let it be enough just to look.

wordCard.voice: Block close. The hidden light of Chagigah: the light of the first day, put away for the righteous, which Hasidic teachers find sown in the Torah and in ordinary life. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: the hidden light, the light of creation stored away.

carryVoice: Your line: the hidden light. Hidden isn't gone; it's sown. One block closes, and another opens tomorrow.
